Fix \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(u\in\{g,\ldots,t\}\).  Because \(P\) is induced by \(Q\), consistency implies
\[
m_{g,1,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\tag{C1}
\]
No effect on ineligible units, followed by consistency, implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
m_{g,0,u}(X)
&=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=g,S=0,X],\\
m_{c,0,u}(X)
&=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C2}
\]
Since \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), one has \(c>t\ge u\).  If \(c\) is finite, mean no anticipation for cohort \(c\), applied at both \(u<c\) and \(u-1<c\), and consistency give
\[
m_{c,1,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X].
\tag{C3}
\]
If \(c=\infty\), (C3) follows directly from consistency.  Define the untreated eligibility gap
\[
B_{a,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=a,S=1,X]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=a,S=0,X].
\]
The conditional parallel-gap assumption applies because \(u\ge g\) and \(c>u\), and hence gives \(B_{g,u}(X)=B_{c,u}(X)\) almost surely.  Using (C1)--(C3) and this equality,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&m_{g,1,u}(X)-m_{g,0,u}(X)-m_{c,1,u}(X)+m_{c,0,u}(X)\\
&\quad=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]\\
&\quad=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)-\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C4}
\]
Summing (C4) over \(u=g,\ldots,t\), using the definition of \(q_{k,c}\), linearity of conditional expectation, and telescoping of the potential-outcome increments yields
\[
q_{k,c}(X)
=E_Q\!\left[
Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)
-\{Y_{g-1}(g,1)-Y_{g-1}(\infty,1)\}
\mathrel{\middle|}G=g,S=1,X\right].
\tag{C5}
\]
Mean no anticipation for the finite target cohort \(g\) at the pretreatment date \(g-1<g\) makes the conditional expectation of the braced term zero.  Therefore
\[
q_{k,c}(X)
=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{C6}
\]
This argument also shows that the right-hand side is independent of the chosen clean comparison \(c\).

Cell overlap and the definition of \(\pi_{g,1}\) give
\[
\pi_{g,1}=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)]\ge\varepsilon>0,
\tag{C7}
\]
so the ratio defining \(\theta_k(P)\) is well defined.  The conditional law of \(X\) given \(G=g,S=1\) has Radon--Nikodym derivative \(p_{g,1}(X)/\pi_{g,1}\) with respect to \(P_X\).  Multiplying (C6) by that derivative and integrating therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_k(P)
&=\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c}(X)]}{\pi_{g,1}}\\
&=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C8}
\]
The asserted formula for \(\tau_\omega(P)\) follows by multiplying (C8) by the prespecified \(\omega_k\), summing over the finite set \(\mathcal K\), and using the definition of \(\tau_\omega\).

Finally, for every cell \((a,s)\), the definition of \(m_{a,s,u}\) gives
\[
E_P[\mathbf 1_{a,s}e_{a,s,k}(O)\mid X]=0.
\tag{C9}
\]
All inverse cell probabilities in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) are finite by overlap.  Hence (C9), the displayed formula for \(R_{k,c,P}\), and (C6) imply
\[
E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)\mid X]
=\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}
\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)\}.
\tag{C10}
\]
More directly, subtracting the ratio-denominator derivative in that definition gives the pointwise identity
\[
\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)
=R_{k,c,P}(O)
-\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\},
\]
which is the claimed centered ratio-functional score.

Suppose first that every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton.  By the definitions of \(M\) and \(K_0\),
\[
M=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}|\mathcal J_k|
=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}1
=|\mathcal K|=K_0.
\tag{K1}
\]
There is exactly one row of \(A\) for each \(k\), and that row has a one in the column indexed by \(k\) and zeros elsewhere.  Thus, after matching the fixed row order to the target order, \(A=I_{K_0}\); under another fixed order, \(A\) is a permutation matrix.  In either case \(A\) is square and nonsingular, so
\[
\ker(A')=\{0\},\qquad M-K_0=0.
\tag{K2}
\]
The definition of \(N\) therefore gives the zero-column matrix, and \(A'b=\omega\) has the unique solution \(b=(A')^{-1}\omega\).  Hence neither the conditional nor the constant program has a comparison-contrast direction.  Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) supplies the source-transcribed two-period, one-target instance of this just-identified reduction, with canonicality only in the finite-support regime stated there.

Now suppose that \(X\) is degenerate.  Conditioning on \(X\) is then conditioning on the trivial sigma-field.  Because the corrected score vector belongs to \(L_2^0(P)^M\), the definitions of \(\Gamma\) and \(\Omega\) give
\[
\Gamma(X)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Psi_P\mid X)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Psi_P)
=E_P[\Psi_P\Psi_P']
=\Omega
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{K3}
\]
Thus the conditional and constant programs minimize the same positive-semidefinite quadratic form over the same affine set.  It remains to show that their singular-case selectors coincide.

Since \(A\) has full column rank, \(b^0=A(A'A)^{-1}\omega\) is feasible.  Every feasible vector has a unique representation
\[
b=b^0+Nz,
\qquad z\in\mathbb R^{M-K_0},
\tag{K4}
\]
because feasibility is equivalent to \(b-b^0\in\ker(A')\), and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of that kernel.  Set
\[
H=N'\Gamma N,
\qquad d=N'\Gamma b^0.
\]
Expanding the common objective in (K4) yields
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)
=(b^0)'\Gamma b^0+2z'd+z'Hz.
\tag{K5}
\]
The matrix \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.  If \(v\in\ker H\), then
\[
0=v'Hv=(Nv)'\Gamma(Nv).
\]
For any \(w\in\mathbb R^M\) and any scalar \(t\), positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
0\le (Nv+tw)'\Gamma(Nv+tw)
=2t w'\Gamma Nv+t^2w'\Gamma w.
\]
If \(w'\Gamma Nv\ne0\), choosing \(t\) with the opposite sign and sufficiently small magnitude would make the right-hand side negative.  Therefore \(w'\Gamma Nv=0\) for every \(w\), so \(\Gamma Nv=0\).  Consequently
\[
v'd=(Nv)'\Gamma b^0=0.
\]
Thus \(d\perp\ker H\).  Since \(H\) is symmetric, \((\ker H)^\perp=\operatorname{range}H\), proving
\[
d\in\operatorname{range}H.
\tag{K6}
\]
The first-order equation for the convex quadratic (K5) is \(Hz=-d\).  By (K6), all and only its solutions are
\[
z=-H^\dagger d+v,
\qquad v\in\ker H.
\tag{K7}
\]
Necessity follows by differentiating (K5).  Conversely, if \(Hz=-d\), then replacing \(z\) by \(z+u\) changes (K5) by \(u'Hu\ge0\), proving sufficiency.

For the conditional selector, the requirement in Definition \(\ref{def:canonical-loading}\) is
\[
N'(b-b^0)=z\in\operatorname{range}H.
\tag{K8}
\]
In (K7), \(-H^\dagger d\in\operatorname{range}H\), while \(v\in\ker H\), and the two subspaces are orthogonal.  Hence (K8) holds if and only if \(v=0\).  Therefore
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0.
\tag{K9}
\]
For the constant selector, \(b^0\in\operatorname{col}A\), whereas \(NH^\dagger d\) and \(Nv\) lie in \(\ker(A')=(\operatorname{col}A)^\perp\).  Orthonormality of the columns of \(N\), together with \(H^\dagger d\perp v\), gives
\[
\|b^0-NH^\dagger d+Nv\|_2^2
=\|b^0\|_2^2+\|H^\dagger d\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{K10}
\]
The unique minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer is therefore obtained at \(v=0\).  By the equivalent argmin characterization in the definition of \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\), (K9) is also \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).  Together with (K3), this proves
\[
b^\star=b^{\mathrm{const}}
\quad\text{when \(X\) is degenerate},
\]
including singular cases.  Formula (K9) agrees with the singular operator representation in Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) whenever its fixed-rank regularity conditions are invoked.

Finally, Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) establishes the only equality claimed here with externally published efficient influence functions from the theorem-level transcriptions of the two panel-DDD results.  At the fixed-finite-support laws specified in that proposition, canonicality in the present observed-law model follows from the tangent exhaustion in Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), rather than from algebraic resemblance.  The proposition makes no tangent-space nesting claim for the separate staggered-DiD result.  This proves the theorem's final qualification.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Consider the two-period, two-cohort specialization with a single target \(k=(g,g)\), a single clean comparison \(\mathcal J_k=\{c\}\), the outcome change \(D=\Delta Y_g\), and unit aggregate weight \(\omega_k=1\). Relabel the target cohort and comparison cohort as \(G_A=1\) and \(G_A=0\), respectively, and relabel eligibility \(S\) as \(D_A\). Then the efficient influence functions in Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's Lemma A.2 and Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 both reduce, term by term, to the core score \(\Psi_{k,c,P}\). Because the relevant published clean set is a singleton, there is no nonzero published OVS normal row and \[\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0=\Psi_{k,c,P}.\] For a scalar aggregate weight \(\omega_k\), all three expressions are multiplied by \(\omega_k\). At every fixed-finite-support conditional-mean-interior law covered by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), this common expression is the exhaustive staggered-DDD canonical gradient, so the two published panel-DDD formulas are exact just-identified special cases there. The algebraic reduction holds independently of that canonicality qualification and does not assert that the staggered-DiD conditional-efficiency model of Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie is nested in, or contains, the eligibility-gap DDD model.

The score identities and the equality \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Psi_{k,c,P}\) are algebraic and remain unrestricted; only their canonical-gradient interpretation is narrowed to the theorem's proved regime.

Write the fixed support as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_J\}\), where \(J<\infty\), and put \(\nu_j=P(X=x_j)\).  The proposed fold-balance condition and the support-mass hypothesis give constants \(c_F,\underline\nu>0\) such that
\[
 |I_\ell^c|\ge c_Fn,
 \qquad
 \min_{1\le j\le J}\nu_j\ge\underline\nu
 \tag{C1}
\]
for every fold and all \(n\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:cell-overlap}\) then gives
\[
 P(X=x_j,G=a,S=s)=\nu_jp_{a,s}(x_j)
 \ge \underline\nu\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \pi_{g,1}=E\{p_{g,1}(X)\}\ge\varepsilon.
 \tag{C2}
\]
Thus every denominator entering Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) is separated from zero.

We first give an explicit description of the cell-frequency implementation.  For each training complement \(I_\ell^c\), form the empirical averages of the finite collection
\[
 \mathbf 1\{X=x_j,G=a,S=s\},\quad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x_j,G=a,S=s\}\Delta Y_u,quad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x_j,G=a,S=s\}\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v,
 \tag{C3}
\]
where \(j,a,s,u,v\) range over their fixed sets, together with the target-cell indicators \(\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}\).  Divide the first-moment averages by the corresponding empirical cell frequencies to obtain \(\widehat m^{-\ell}\), use the empirical conditional cell shares for \(\widehat p^{-\ell}\), and use the empirical target shares for \(\widehat\pi^{-\ell}\).  Substitute these quantities in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), including its ratio correction, and take within-\(X\)-cell empirical first and second moments of that score.  Their difference is \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)\).  On the event that an empirical denominator is smaller than half its population lower bound in (C2), define the corresponding ratio arbitrarily; the probability of this event tends to zero at the rate established below.  This makes the estimator a total measurable map of the training sample.

For every retained cell and period, Assumption \(\ref{ass:conditional-fourth-envelope}\) and the elementary conditional inequality
\[
 |E(\Delta Y_u\mid G=a,S=s,X)|^4
 \le E(|\Delta Y_u|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X)
 \tag{C4}
\]
bound \(m_{a,s,u}(X)\) uniformly.  Because \(T\), \(\mathcal G\), and \(\mathcal I\) are fixed and (C2) bounds every inverse propensity and target share, Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and \(|z_1+\cdots+z_d|^4\le d^3\sum_h|z_h|^4\) imply
\[
 \sup_{1\le j\le J}E\{\|\Psi_P(O)\|^4\mid X=x_j\}<\infty.
 \tag{C5}
\]
Moreover, for any two periods,
\[
 E\{(\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v)^2\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_j\}
 \le
 E(|\Delta Y_u|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_j)^{1/2}
 E(|\Delta Y_v|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_j)^{1/2},
 \tag{C6}
\]
so every variable in (C3) has finite variance, uniformly over the fixed index set.

Let \(\mu\) be the finite vector of population moments in (C3) and the target shares, and let \(\widehat\mu^{-\ell}\) be its training-sample version.  Independence in Assumption \(\ref{ass:crossfit-independence}\) is not needed for this within-training calculation, but ensures that the same quantities may subsequently be evaluated on \(I_\ell\).  For every coordinate \(Z) of (C3), independence of the sampled units and (C1) give
\[
 E\!\left[\left\{|I_\ell^c|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_\ell^c}(Z_i-EZ)\right\}^2\right]
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Z)}{|I_\ell^c|}
 \le \frac{C}{n}.
 \tag{C7}
\]
Consequently, for every \(K>0\), applying \(P(U^2>K^2)\le E(U^2)/K^2\) coordinatewise and summing over the fixed numbers of coordinates and folds yields
\[
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat\mu^{-\ell}-\mu\|
 =O_P(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{C8}
\]
In particular, (C8) and (C2) show that all empirical denominators exceed half their population lower bounds with probability tending to one.

For each \(x_j\), the substitutions following (C3) express \(\Gamma_P(x_j)\) as a finite rational map \(F_j(\mu)\), and express \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)\) as the same map \(F_j(\widehat\mu^{-\ell})\).  This statement includes estimation of \(q\), \(\theta\), and the correction for \(\pi_{g,1}\): each is obtained from the same finite first-moment and share vector.  By (C2), all denominators of \(F_j\) are bounded away from zero.  On a fixed neighborhood of \(\mu\), its finitely many partial derivatives are therefore bounded by a constant \(C_F\).  The coordinatewise fundamental theorem of calculus and (C8) give
\[
 \max_{\ell,j}
 \|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)-\Gamma(x_j)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_F\max_\ell\|\widehat\mu^{-\ell}-\mu\|
 =O_P(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{C9}
\]
Since the support and matrix dimension are fixed,
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
 =\max_\ell\left\{\sum_{j=1}^J\nu_j
 \|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)-\Gamma(x_j)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^4\right\}^{1/4}
 =O_P(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{C10}
\]
The rate sequences \(r_{p,n}\) and \(r_{m,n}\) are nonnegative, so (C10) implies the displayed \(O_P(n^{-1/2}+r_{p,n}+r_{m,n})\) assertion.  The construction in (C3) also proves the assertion that every conditional moment in the correctly specified one-step construction is estimated by its corresponding cell average.  Applying the same ratio argument to the first moments shows that the cell propensity and regression first stages are \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).

Set \(r_{\Gamma,n}=n^{-1/2}\) up to a fixed multiplicative constant.  Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:fixed-contrast-rank}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\), if \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) with \(0<a<1/4\), then Assumptions \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-vanishing}\) and \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-separation}\) hold because
\[
 \tau_n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{C11}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:loading-perturbation}\), applied using (C10), therefore gives consistent rank recovery and
\[
 r_{b,n}=\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}=O(n^{-1/2+a}),
 \qquad
 r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2
 =O(n^{-1+2a}+n^{-1})=o(n^{-1/2}),
 \tag{C12}
\]
where the last equality uses \(a<1/4\).

For completeness, the final continuous-covariate qualification has a generic-class certificate.  Fix one coordinate \((k,c)\), with \(k=(g,t)\), take \(X\) uniform on \([0,1]\), and make \((G,S)\) independent of \(X\) with fixed probabilities \(p^0_{a,s}\ge\varepsilon\).  Put all conditional increment means equal to zero.  In cell \((g,1)\), set only \(\Delta Y_g=\{v_\beta(X)\}^{1/2}Z\), where \(Z\) is an independent Rademacher variable; set all other increments and cells equal to zero.  Here a known partition \((B_j)_{j=1}^{m}\) divides \([0,1]\) into equal intervals and
\[
 v_\beta(x)=1+\delta\beta_j\quad\text{for }x\in B_j,
 \qquad \beta_j\in\{0,1\},\qquad 0<\delta<1.
 \tag{C13}
\]
These laws satisfy overlap and the conditional fourth-moment envelope; their conditional means are zero, so any restrictions on those means are also satisfied.  Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives, for the chosen diagonal coordinate,
\[
 \Gamma_{(k,c),(k,c)}(x)=\frac{v_\beta(x)}{p^0_{g,1}}.
 \tag{C14}
\]
Give the bits \(\beta_j\) independent fair Bernoulli priors.  Whatever estimator is used, at most \(n\) of the \(m\) intervals contain a sampled \(X_i\).  Conditional on the data, every bit belonging to an unvisited interval remains fair.  If the two possible values in (C14) are denoted by \(u\) and \(u+d\), where \(d=\delta/p^0_{g,1}>0\), then for every real \(a\),
\[
 \frac12\{|a-u|^4+|a-u-d|^4\}\ge\frac{d^4}{16}.
 \tag{C15}
\]
Taking \(m=2n\), integrating over a fresh \(X\), and then averaging over the bits and the sample gives, for every estimator \(\widetilde\Gamma\),
\[
 \sup_{\beta\in\{0,1\}^{2n}}
 E_\beta\!\left[
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma_\beta\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
 \right]
 \ge \left(1-\frac{n}{2n}\right)\frac{d^4}{16}
 =\frac{d^4}{32}.
 \tag{C16}
\]
Indeed, operator-norm error dominates the absolute error of the diagonal entry (C14).  Truncating that entry to \([u,u+d]\) cannot increase its loss and makes the fourth-power loss bounded; hence (C16) also rules out uniform convergence in probability.  Thus a continuous-(X\) \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance rate cannot follow from overlap and a fourth-moment envelope alone: smoothness or other structure in \(x\) is genuinely necessary.

For a fold \(\ell\), write
\[
 \widetilde H_\ell(x)=N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N,
 \qquad
 E_\ell(x)=\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)-\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
 \tag{B1}
\]
Because \(N'N=I\),
\[
 \|\widetilde H_\ell(x)-H(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le E_\ell(x).
 \tag{B2}
\]
For every unit vector \(v\), the absolute difference between the Rayleigh quotients of \(\widetilde H_\ell(x)\) and \(H(x)\) is at most \(E_\ell(x)\).  Taking the successive minima and maxima in the variational characterization of the ordered eigenvalues therefore gives
\[
 \max_j|\lambda_j\{\widetilde H_\ell(x)\}-\lambda_j\{H(x)\}|
 \le E_\ell(x).
 \tag{B3}
\]
By Assumptions \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-vanishing}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\), \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Assumptions \(\ref{ass:fixed-contrast-rank}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\) say that \(H(x)\) has exactly \(r_0\) eigenvalues in \([\kappa,\kappa^{-1}]\) and all its other eigenvalues are zero, for almost every \(x\).  Hence (B3) shows that
\[
 \{\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)\ne r_0\}\subseteq\{E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\}.
 \tag{B4}
\]
Indeed, a retained eigenvalue from the zero cluster requires \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\), whereas failure to retain a positive population eigenvalue requires \(E_\ell(x)\ge\kappa-\tau_n>\tau_n\).  Conditional on the training sample, the elementary bound \(P_X(U>t)\le t^{-4}E_X(U^4)\), Assumption \(\ref{ass:covariance-rate}\), and fixed \(L\) now yield
\[
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}
 \le \tau_n^{-4}\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
 =O_P\!\left\{\left(\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}\right)^4\right\}.
 \tag{B5}
\]
This proves the rank statement, including its uniformity over the fixed folds.

It remains to control the loading.  By Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), with
\[
 g(x)=N'\Gamma(x)b^0,
 \qquad
 z^0(x)=H(x)^\dagger g(x),
 \tag{B6}
\]
one has \(g(x)\in\operatorname{range}H(x)\), \(H(x)z^0(x)=g(x)\), and
\[
 b^\star(x)=b^0-Nz^0(x).
 \tag{B7}
\]
The moment conditions invoked here also make the constants below uniform in \(x\).  In fact, Assumption \(\ref{ass:cell-overlap}\) implies \(\pi_{g,1}\ge\varepsilon\) and bounds every propensity ratio in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:conditional-fourth-envelope}\), the fixed horizon, and \(|z_1+\cdots+z_d|^4\le d^3\sum_h|z_h|^4\) then give
\[
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x}E\{\|\Psi_P(O)\|^4\mid X=x\}<\infty.
 \tag{B8}
\]
Thus \(\sup_x\|\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty\).  Since every positive eigenvalue of \(H(x)\) is at least \(\kappa\), (B6) implies
\[
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x}\|z^0(x)\|
 \le \kappa^{-1}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x}\|N'\Gamma(x)b^0\|<\infty;
 \tag{B9}
\]
the inequality is also valid under the zero-rank convention, when \(z^0=0\).

Let \(\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)\) retain exactly the eigencomponents of \(\widetilde H_\ell(x)\) whose eigenvalues exceed \(\tau_n\), and put
\[
 \widehat P_{\ell,\tau}(x)
 =\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)^\dagger\widetilde H_\ell(x),
 \qquad
 P_H(x)=H(x)^\dagger H(x),
 \qquad
 \widehat g_\ell(x)=N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)b^0.
 \tag{B10}
\]
These are the orthogonal projectors onto the retained empirical space and \(\operatorname{range}H(x)\), respectively.  Spectral truncation gives
\[
 \|\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\tau_n^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat g_\ell(x)-g(x)\|
 \le \|b^0\|E_\ell(x).
 \tag{B11}
\]
Using \(g=Hz^0\) and the fact that the truncated inverse annihilates the discarded empirical eigenvectors gives the exact identity
\[
 \widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}^\dagger\widehat g_\ell
 =\widehat P_{\ell,\tau}z^0
 +\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}^\dagger
 \{(H-\widetilde H_\ell)z^0+(\widehat g_\ell-g)\}.
 \tag{B12}
\]

We next bound the projector term without assuming rank recovery.  If \(E_\ell(x)\le\tau_n\), (B3) and \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\) show that the retained empirical space has dimension \(r_0\).  If \(\widehat u\) is a unit retained empirical eigenvector with eigenvalue \(\widehat\lambda\), then \(\widehat\lambda\ge\kappa-E_\ell(x)\).  Multiplying
\(\widetilde H_\ell\widehat u=\widehat\lambda\widehat u\)
by \(I-P_H\), using \((I-P_H)H=0\), and applying (B2) yields
\[
 \|(I-P_H)\widehat u\|
 \le\frac{E_\ell(x)}{\kappa-E_\ell(x)}.
 \tag{B13}
\]
 Applying this bound to an orthonormal basis of the retained space, using equality of the two ranks, and bounding the operator norm by the Frobenius norm bounds both off-diagonal blocks of the two projectors; in particular,
\[
 \|\widehat P_{\ell,\tau}(x)-P_H(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{2\sqrt{r_0}\,E_\ell(x)}{\kappa-E_\ell(x)}.
\tag{B14}
\]
If \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\), the difference of two orthogonal projectors has norm at most two, and hence at most \(2E_\ell(x)/\tau_n\).  Combining the two cases, using \(P_Hz^0=z^0\), (B9), (B11), and (B12), gives a fixed constant \(C\) such that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)-b^\star(x)\|
 &=\|N\{\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)^\dagger\widehat g_\ell(x)-z^0(x)\}\|\\
 &\le C\frac{E_\ell(x)}{\tau_n}
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{B15}
\]
for almost every \(x\) and all sufficiently large \(n\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:covariance-rate}\) therefore implies
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^\star\|_{P_X,4}
 \le C\tau_n^{-1}max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
 =O_P\!\left(\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}\right).
 \tag{B16}
\]
Because \(P_X\) is a probability measure, \(\|f\|_{P_X,2}\le\|f\|_{P_X,4}\), so the same rate holds in \(L_2(P_X)\).  By the definition of \(r_{b,n}\) and Assumption \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-separation}\), (B16) is \(O_P(r_{b,n})=o_P(1)\).

Finally, the sharper assertion concerns the consistently selected spectral region
\[
 \mathcal A_{\ell n}=\{x:E_\ell(x)\le\tau_n\}.
 \tag{B17}
\]
On this region, (B3) selects exactly the population positive cluster, its retained eigenvalues are at least \(\kappa-\tau_n\ge\kappa/2\), and (B11) improves to \(\|\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\kappa\).  Equations (B12)--(B14) then give
\[
 \max_\ell
 \|\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_{\ell n}}(\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^\star)\|_{P_X,4}
 \le C\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
 =O_P(r_{\Gamma,n}),
 \tag{B18}
\]
which is the claimed sharper local bound on the consistently selected spectral range.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
If \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, and if the fixed-\(L\) folds satisfy \(\min_{1\le\ell\le L}|I_\ell^c|\ge c_Fn\) for some fixed \(c_F>0\), the foldwise cell-frequency estimator of the corrected shared-cell covariance \(\Gamma_P(X)=\operatorname{Cov}_P\{\Psi_P(O)\mid X\}\) satisfies
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
=O_P(n^{-1/2}+r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}).
\]
All conditional expectations used in a correctly specified one-step construction are estimated by the corresponding cell averages. If, in addition, contrast rank is fixed and its positive spectrum is separated, parametric first stages and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) with \(0<a<1/4\) give consistent rank recovery, \(r_{\Gamma,n}=O(n^{-1/2})\), and \(r_{b,n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\), with \(r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2=o(n^{-1/2})\). The continuous-covariate \(L_4(P_X)\) rate in the original statement does not follow from only a conditional fourth moment for outcomes.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The displayed root-\(n\) rate requires every training complement to contain order \(n\) observations. Fixed \(L\) by itself does not imply this: for example, a two-fold partition may have one training complement of size one. The added fold-balance condition is an estimator-side sampling condition, not a restriction on the observed-law model, and the rest of the claim is unchanged.

proposed.statement: Let \(\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)=\#\{j:\lambda_j(N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N)>\tau_n\}\), and form \(\widehat H^{-\ell}\) and \(\widehat b^{-\ell}\) from the retained eigencomponents. Under fixed rank, separated positive spectrum, \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance error, and \(r_{\Gamma,n}=o(\tau_n)\), \(P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}=O_P\{(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)^4\}\) uniformly over folds. The thresholded Moore--Penrose perturbation and its projector obey \[\max_{\ell}\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^{\star}\|_{P_X,2}+\max_{\ell}\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^{\star}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(r_{b,n})=o_P(1),\qquad r_{b,n}=r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n.\] On the consistently selected spectral range the sharper local bound is \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n})\). Thus both rank recovery and the loading rate are derived from covariance learning and threshold separation rather than supplied by an oracle rank or a standalone loading assumption.
proposed.justification: The learned loading rate must follow from covariance estimation and stable quotient geometry rather than being assumed as an independent first-stage property.
proposed.gap: Standard Moore--Penrose perturbation bounds do not by themselves control the DDD loading in \(L_4(P_X)\); the conditional moment envelope and the affine fixed-rank construction close that step.
proposed.consumer: The result supplies the loading remainder bound used by both the efficient estimator and the efficiency-gap estimator.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the displayed joint-score formula to derive the uniform conditional fourth-moment and covariance bounds needed for the pseudoinverse perturbation. Adding Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) makes that load-bearing dependency explicit; the claim and all other metadata are unchanged.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write the fixed support as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\), and put \(\nu_d=P(X=x_d)\).  The asserted lower support-mass bound and retained-cell overlap imply
\[
P(X=x_d,G=a,S=s)=\nu_d p_{a,s}(x_d)\ge \underline\nu\varepsilon>0
\tag{37a}
\]
for every retained \((d,a,s)\).  Under the stated fixed-fold construction, every training complement contains order \(n\) observations.  For any one of the finitely many cell variables \(W\) used below, let \(\widehat E_{-\ell}[W\mid a,s,x_d]\) denote its training-cell mean.  Conditional fourth moments of \(\Delta Y_u\), retained-cell overlap, and fixed \(T\) imply finite second moments for: indicators; indicator-weighted increments; products of two increments; and every fixed finite linear combination of these variables.  Chebyshev's inequality applied to their empirical numerators and denominators, followed by the elementary ratio identity
\[
\frac{A_n}{B_n}-\frac{A}{B}
=\frac{A_n-A}{B_n}+\frac{A(B-B_n)}{BB_n},
\tag{37b}
\]
on the event \(B_n\ge B/2\), proves, uniformly over the finite sets of folds, support points, cells, periods, and coordinates,
\[
\widehat p_{a,s}^{-\ell}(x_d)-p_{a,s}(x_d)=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
\qquad
\widehat m_{a,s,u}^{-\ell}(x_d)-m_{a,s,u}(x_d)=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{37c}
\]
The same argument gives the root-\(n\) rate for every training preliminary target ratio and every empirical conditional raw moment of degree at most two in the increments.  Since \(D\) and all vector dimensions are fixed,
\[
\|f\|_{P_X,4}\le \max_{1\le d\le D}|f(x_d)|
\tag{37d}
\]
coordinatewise, so the same rates hold in all displayed \(L_4(P_X)\) norms.

We next pass from the primitive cell moments to the two learned conditional moments.  On the event supplied by (37a)--(37c), all clipped reciprocals are bounded by \(2/\varepsilon\).  The explicit formulas in Definitions \(\ref{def:orthogonal-ovs-normal-signal}\) and \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) are then finite sums and products of the empirical quantities in (37c), bounded reciprocals, and conditional raw moments of degree at most two.  Repeated use of
\[
ab-a_0b_0=(a-a_0)b_0+a_0(b-b_0)+(a-a_0)(b-b_0)
\tag{37e}
\]
shows entry by entry that
\[
\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d)-K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)
=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
\qquad
\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d)-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)
=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{37f}
\]
This calculation includes the off-diagonal products of score coordinates sharing an outcome cell; they are empirical cross-products in (37e), not omitted blockwise terms.  Taking the finite maximum, using equivalence of finite-dimensional matrix norms, and applying (37d) proves (37).

It remains to justify thresholding and the coefficient rate, including singular cases.  Fix a support point and abbreviate
\[
K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d),\quad
\widehat K=\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d),\quad
r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d),\quad
\widehat r=\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d).
\]
Both \(K\) and \(\widehat K\) are symmetric positive semidefinite second-moment matrices.  For ordered eigenvalues, the variational characterization of eigenvalues and the inequality \(|v'(\widehat K-K)v|\le\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) for \(\|v\|=1\) give
\[
|\lambda_j(\widehat K)-\lambda_j(K)|
\le\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{38a}
\]
At the fixed law, the minimum over all positive eigenvalues of all \(K(x_d)\) is a strictly positive number \(\delta_P\), with the zero-rank convention if no such eigenvalue exists.  Since \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\) and \(\tau_n\to0\), (38a) implies simultaneously over the finite support and folds that every population zero eigenvalue is below \(\tau_n\) and every positive eigenvalue is above \(\tau_n\), with probability tending to one.  This proves rank recovery.

The population right-hand side is compatible with the singular system.  Indeed, if \(v\in\ker K\), then
\[
0=v'Kv=E_P[(v'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}})^2\mid X=x_d],
\]
so \(v'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=0\) conditionally almost surely and consequently \(v'r=E_P[v'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\psi_P^0\mid X=x_d]=0\).  Thus \(r\in\operatorname{range}K\), and \(\alpha=K^\dagger r\) is the unique solution in \(\operatorname{range}K\).

At a support point where \(K\) has rank zero, rank recovery makes the retained matrix zero, so \(\widehat\alpha=\alpha=0\) and the coefficient-rate conclusion is immediate.  Consider a positive-rank support point.  On the rank-recovery event let \(\Pi\) and \(\widehat\Pi\) be the orthogonal projectors onto the ranges of \(K\) and the retained \(\widehat K\).  When \(\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\delta_P/4\), every retained eigenvalue is at least \(\delta_P/2\).  If \(\widehat u\) is a retained unit eigenvector and \(Q=I-\Pi\), then
\[
\lambda(\widehat K)Q\widehat u
=Q\widehat K\widehat u
=Q(\widehat K-K)\widehat u,
\]
because \(QK=0\).  Hence \(\|Q\widehat u\|\le 2\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}/\delta_P\).  Applying this to a retained orthonormal basis, and using equality of the two nonzero principal-angle spectra for equal-rank subspaces, gives
\[
\|\widehat\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le C_P\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{38b}
\]
This is an elementary consequence of the displayed eigenvector equation, rather than an extra rank or spectral assumption.

Since \(\|\widehat K_\tau^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\delta_P\) on this event and \(\widehat K_\tau^\dagger\widehat K=\widehat\Pi\), the identities \(r=K\alpha\) and \(\Pi\alpha=\alpha\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\alpha-\alpha
&=\widehat K_\tau^\dagger(\widehat r-r)
+\widehat K_\tau^\dagger(K-\widehat K)\alpha
+(\widehat\Pi-\Pi)\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{38c}
\]
Equations (37f), (38b), and (38c) yield \(\widehat\alpha-\alpha=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) at each support point.  The finite maximum and (37d) give the stated sharper \(L_4(P_X)\) rate uniformly over folds.  Since \(\tau_n\le1\) eventually, this sharper fixed-law statement also implies the conservative bound
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}
-K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n),
\]
which is (38).  If \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), the right side is \(O_P(n^{-1/2+a})\); its square is \(O_P(n^{-1+2a})=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) for \(a<1/4\), and its product with either rate in (37c) is \(O_P(n^{-1+a})=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) for the same range.  This proves all assertions.

Let \(\eta=(p,m)\), and define the population projection coefficient and uncentered reference score by
\[
\alpha_P(x)=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x),
\qquad
\mu_P(O)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k R_{k,c_0(k),P}(O).
\tag{41a}
\]
Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) gives every published observable equality, and Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-orthogonal-normal-signal}\) therefore gives
\[
S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\eta)=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O),
\qquad E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\mid X]=0.
\tag{41b}
\]
The fixed support-mass lower bound, retained-cell overlap, independent fixed-\(T\) sampling, and the conditional fourth-moment envelope give the root-\(n\) finite-cell rates derived in Proposition \(\ref{prop:ovs-normal-finite-support-rates}\).  With \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\), that proposition also gives, uniformly over the fixed number of folds,
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}-\alpha_P\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2+a})=o_P(1).
\tag{41c}
\]

We first expand the cross-fitted ratio part.  For \(k=(g,t)\), put
\[
M_{a,s,k}(x)=\sum_{u=g}^t m_{a,s,u}(x),
\qquad
\widehat M_{a,s,k}^{-\ell}(x)=\sum_{u=g}^t\widehat m_{a,s,u}^{-\ell}(x),
\]
and let \(B_{k,c,P}\) denote the bracketed numerator in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), so \(R_{k,c,P}=B_{k,c,P}/\pi_{g,1}\).  Conditional on the training complement, direct addition and subtraction of the true regressions in the estimated bracket gives the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}^{-\ell}-B_{k,c,P}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]
={}&\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}^{-\ell}p_{g,0}}{\widehat p_{g,0}^{-\ell}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{g,0,k}^{-\ell}-M_{g,0,k})\\
&+\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}^{-\ell}p_{c,1}}{\widehat p_{c,1}^{-\ell}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,1,k}^{-\ell}-M_{c,1,k})\\
&+\left(p_{g,1}-\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}^{-\ell}p_{c,0}}{\widehat p_{c,0}^{-\ell}}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,0,k}^{-\ell}-M_{c,0,k}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{41d}
\]
There is no \((g,1)\) regression-error term because the plug-in conditional contrast and the treated-cell residual in the first bracket cancel it algebraically.  Clipping and overlap make each coefficient in parentheses Lipschitz in \(\widehat p^{-\ell}-p\).  The finite-cell root-\(n\) rates and H\"older's inequality consequently imply
\[
\|E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}^{-\ell}-B_{k,c,P}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}
=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\|\widehat B_{k,c}^{-\ell}-B_{k,c,P}\|_{P,2}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41e}
\]
The second bound follows by expanding the displayed score formula: every coefficient error is root-\(n\), all inverse propensities are bounded, and every residual has a bounded conditional second moment by the conditional fourth-moment envelope.

By fixed-fold cross-fitting, conditional on \(\mathcal D_{-\ell}\) the validation observations in \(I_\ell\) are independent of the estimated functions used there.  Conditional Chebyshev inequality applied to the centered difference in (41e), followed by summation over the fixed number of folds, yields
\[
\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\widehat B_{i,k,c}^{-\ell}
=P B_{k,c,P}+(\mathbb P_n-P)B_{k,c,P}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41f}
\]
Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives \(P B_{k,c,P}=\pi_{g,1}\theta_k(P)\).  Also, retained-cell overlap implies \(\pi_{g,1}>0\), while independent sampling and finite variance give \(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1}=O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  The exact scalar expansion
\[
\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-1}-\pi_{g,1}^{-1}
=-\pi_{g,1}^{-2}(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})
+\frac{(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})^2}
{\pi_{g,1}^2\widehat\pi_{g,1}}
\tag{41g}
\]
has an \(O_P(n^{-1})\) remainder.  Combining (41f)--(41g), and using
\(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1}=(\mathbb P_n-P)\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}\), proves
\[
\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{\ell}\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat B_{i,k,c}^{-\ell}}
{\widehat\pi_{g,1}}-\theta_k(P)
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\left\{
R_{k,c,P}-\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}
\right\}+o_P(n^{-1/2})
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\Psi_{k,c,P}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41h}
\]
Thus the global empirical share contributes exactly the denominator-derivative term in the corrected score; it is not absorbed into an uncorrected centering.

We next expand the complete-normal correction.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-orthogonal-normal-signal}\), the root-\(n\) cell rates, and (41b) imply
\[
\|E_P[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}
=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\|\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}-Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{P,2}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41i}
\]
The finite-support population coefficient \(\alpha_P\) is finite at every support point under the Moore--Penrose convention.  Equations (41c), (41i), H\"older's inequality, and the conditional fourth-moment envelope therefore give
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X)'
\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
-\alpha_P(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{P,2}=o_P(1).
\tag{41j}
\]
Moreover, (41i) and \(\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}=O_P(1)\) make the conditional expectation of the first product in (41j) \(O_P(n^{-1})\), whereas the expectation of the second product is zero by (41b).  Cross-fit independence and conditional Chebyshev inequality now show
\[
\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X_i)'
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
=\mathbb P_n\{\alpha_P(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41k}
\]

Summing (41h) at \(c=c_0(k)\) with the fixed weights \(\omega_k\), and subtracting (41k), proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
&=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\left\{\psi_P^0(O_i)-\alpha_P(X_i)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O_i)\right\}+o_P(1)\\
&=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)+o_P(1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{41l}
\]
where the second equality is Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\).  The summands are independent and identically distributed by the sampling assumption, have mean zero by (41b) and the ambient-gradient centering, and are square integrable by overlap and the fourth-moment condition.  Their variance is \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\) by the theorem's positivity hypothesis.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\) applied to (41l) proves (41).

For variance consistency, let \(\widehat\phi_i\) be the displayed quantity in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\), and let \(\phi_i=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)\).  Equations (37c), (41c), (41i), the ratio expansion (41g), and \(\widehat\theta_k-\theta_k=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), which follows from (41h), imply foldwise
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat\phi_i-\phi_i)^2=o_P(1).
\tag{42a}
\]
To see this without an empirical-process assumption, condition one fold at a time on its training complement, apply Markov's inequality to the nonnegative squared difference using its \(o_P(1)\) conditional mean, and sum over the fixed number of folds; the global shares and preliminary ratios are finite-dimensional root-\(n\) terms and hence do not alter the conclusion.  By Cauchy--Schwarz, (42a) gives
\[
\left|\mathbb P_n\widehat\phi^2-\mathbb P_n\phi^2\right|
\le \{\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi)^2\}^{1/2}
\{2\mathbb P_n\phi^2+2\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi)^2\}^{1/2}
=o_P(1).
\tag{42b}
\]
The ordinary law of large numbers applies to \(\phi_i^2\), which is integrable, and gives \(\mathbb P_n\phi^2\to_P V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Also \(|\mathbb P_n\widehat\phi-\mathbb P_n\phi|\le\{\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi)^2\}^{1/2}=o_P(1)\), while \(\mathbb P_n\phi=o_P(1)\).  Expanding the centered empirical second moment in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) therefore proves
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\longrightarrow_P V_{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\tag{42c}
\]
Because \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\), (42c) makes the estimated standard deviation divided by \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{OVS}}}\) converge to one.  Combining this fact with (41), and sandwiching the studentized statistic between Gaussian continuity points, yields
\[
P\{\tau_\omega(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Finally, Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), whose finite-support and conditional-mean-interior hypotheses are imposed here, identifies \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) as the canonical gradient in the published OVS observed-law tangent space and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) as its pointwise efficiency bound.  Hence the explicit cross-fitted estimator attains that bound at the fixed law.  The same theorem and Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) give \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\mathcal T_P\), so the localized canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\), which represents the derivative on \(\mathcal T_P\), also represents it on every published score and is therefore a valid regular gradient on the published subclass.  Its variance satisfies
\[
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2],
\]
again by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\).  Thus a regular estimator with the localized influence function attains the published bound exactly when the displayed squared distance vanishes, equivalently when the conditional published-normal equation in that theorem holds; otherwise its variance is strictly larger.  Every step used fixed support and a fixed-law positive spectrum after threshold recovery; none establishes continuous-covariate, rank-uniform, or equality-boundary inference.

Fix one of the two declared comparators and abbreviate \(b=b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\).  First note from Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) that the cell-residual terms have conditional mean zero.  Hence, for \((k,c)\in\mathcal I\), with \(k=(g,t)\),
\[
 E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)\mid X]
 =\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)\}
 =h_k(X).
\tag{E7}
\]
The last equality uses the observable clean-comparison equality, under which \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\).  Both \(b\) and \(b^\star(X)\) are feasible, so \(A'b=A'b^\star(X)=\omega\).  It follows from (E7) that
\[
 E_P[b'\Psi_P\mid X]=E_P[b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\mid X]=\omega'h(X).
\tag{E8}
\]
The definition of \(\theta_k(P)\) also gives \(E_P[h_k(X)]=0\), so both scores in (E8) are mean zero.
Consequently the conditional-variance identity and the definition of \(\Gamma\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(b'\Psi_P)-\operatorname{Var}_P(b^{\star\prime}\Psi_P)
 =E_P[b'\Gamma_P(X)b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^\star].
\tag{E9}
\]

Because the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\), there is a measurable vector \(z(X)\) such that
\[
 d(X):=b-b^\star(X)=Nz(X).
\tag{E10}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^\star(X)=0\).  Expanding the integrand in (E9) therefore yields, pointwise,
\[
 b'\Gamma b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma b^\star
 =2d'\Gamma b^\star+d'\Gamma d
 =z'H z
 =(b-b^\star)'\Gamma(b-b^\star).
\tag{E11}
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}=\operatorname{Var}_P(b^{\star\prime}\Psi_P)\), integration of (E11) proves (E1).  Adding the defining identities
\[
 V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{can}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P),
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}(P)
\tag{E12}
\]
proves (E2) and (E3).

For the first equality characterization, again use (E10) and Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) to obtain
\[
 N'\Gamma_P(X)b
 =N'\Gamma_P(X)\{b-b^\star(X)\}
 =H(X)z(X).
\tag{E13}
\]
If (E13) vanishes, the integrand \(z'Hz\) in (E11) vanishes.  Conversely, equality in (E1) implies \(E_P[z'Hz]=0\).  The integrand is nonnegative because \(H=N'\Gamma N\) is positive semidefinite, so \(z'H z=0\) almost surely.  For a positive semidefinite matrix, \(z'Hz=\|H^{1/2}z\|^2=0\) implies \(Hz=0\); (E13) then vanishes.  This proves (E4), including singular cases.

It remains to distinguish the two model-normal equations.  Let \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) denote the closed measurable spans generated by \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), respectively.  If \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) puts weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on the other coordinates, then \(A'b^{\mathrm{ref}}=\omega\) and \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\).  Thus \(b-b^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\ker(A')\).  Within a target block, the denominator-correction terms cancel, so
\[
 (b-b^{\mathrm{ref}})'\Psi_P=(b-b^{\mathrm{ref}})'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{E14}
\]
For a single comparison replacement, direct subtraction in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives
\[
 \Psi_{k,c,P}-\Psi_{k,c_0(k),P}
 =-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}
   \sum_{u=g}^{t} Z_{(u,c,c_0(k)),P}.
\tag{E15}
\]
Every formal row on the right of (E15) is in the row span defining \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\).  Moreover, both \(c\) and \(c_0(k)\) exceed \(t\ge u\), so each such row is also an OVS row.  Linear decomposition within each target block, followed by closure, therefore proves
\[
 \mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}
 \subseteq\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\tag{E16}
\]

We next verify the projection formulas, including singular cases.  For either normal vector \(Z\), write
\[
 K(X)=E_P[ZZ'\mid X],\qquad r(X)=E_P[Z\psi_P^0\mid X].
\]
If \(v\in\ker K(X)\), then
\[
 E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X]=v'K(X)v=0,
\]
and hence \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(v'r(X)=0\).  Thus \(r(X)\in\operatorname{range}K(X)\), and
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z\{\psi_P^0-r(X)'K(X)^\dagger Z\}\mid X\right]
 =r(X)-K(X)K(X)^\dagger r(X)=0.
\tag{E17}
\]
Moreover, with \(\alpha=K^\dagger r\), expansion of the nonnegative conditional square \(E_P[(\psi_P^0-\alpha'Z)^2\mid X]\) shows that \(r'K^\dagger r\le E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2\mid X]\); hence the displayed projection is square-integrable.  Equation (E17), first for bounded measurable multipliers and then for their \(L_2(P)\) closure, proves that \(r'K^\dagger Z\) is the orthogonal projection of \(\psi_P^0\) onto the corresponding normal span.  Therefore \(\phi_{\mathrm{can}}\) is orthogonal to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}\), and \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) is orthogonal to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  In the fixed-finite-support conditional-mean-interior regime, Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) identifies these spans with the respective tangent orthocomplements, and Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) identifies the residuals with the corresponding canonical gradients.

Put \(g=b'\Psi_P\).  By (E14)--(E16), \(g-\psi_P^0\) belongs to each relevant normal span.  Orthogonal decomposition using (E17) consequently gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(g)-V_{\mathrm{can}}
 =\|g-\phi_{\mathrm{can}}\|_{L_2(P)}^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(g)-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 =\|g-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{L_2(P)}^2.
\tag{E18}
\]
The first difference in (E18) is zero exactly when \(g\perp\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}\), and the second is zero exactly when \(g\perp\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  For a finite-dimensional conditional normal vector, orthogonality to every square-integrable measurable multiple of \(Z\) is equivalent to
\[
 E_P[Zg\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely};
\tag{E19}
\]
the forward implication follows by the defining property of conditional expectation, and the reverse implication follows by testing against bounded measurable multipliers and truncating.  Applying (E19) to the two normal vectors proves (E5) and (E6).  Together with (E4), these are precisely the three residuals reported in Definition \(\ref{def:projection-diagnostic}\).

The construction gives
\[
 p_{a,s}(x)=\frac16
 \quad\text{for every }a\in\{2,3,\infty\},\ s\in\{0,1\},\ x\in\{-1,1\},
 \qquad \pi_{2,1}=\frac16.
\tag{Q1}
\]
Because \(|(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})/8|\le 1/4\) and \(|\delta|<1/8\),
\[
 \max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|
 \le \frac14+|\delta|<\frac38.
\tag{Q2}
\]
Consistency holds by the last clause of Definition \(\ref{def:binary-witness}\).  If \(s=0\), the treatment term in that definition is zero at every date, proving no effect on ineligible units.  If \(u<a\), then \(Y_u(a,1)=Y_u(\infty,1)=Z_u^{\mathrm w}\), proving no anticipation.  Conditional on \((G,X)\), the law of \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\) does not depend on \(S\).  Therefore every untreated within-cohort eligibility gap is zero, so both sides of every global conditional parallel-gap restriction in Definition \(\ref{def:target-model}\) are zero.  Hence \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

Since \(r<\sqrt7/3<1\), each conditional sign probability \(\{1+\rho_a(x)uv\}/4\) is strictly positive.  In every cohort--eligibility cell the conditional support of \((\Delta Y_2,\Delta Y_3)\) is therefore the four vertices of a translated square.  Both signs have conditional mean zero, so the conditional mean is the translated center, which is in the relative interior of that square.  Thus the induced observed law is conditional-mean interior.  Equation (Q1) supplies overlap, (Q2) supplies the fourth-moment condition, and the two values of \(X\) have positive probability.

The observed increments are
\[
 \Delta Y_2=\frac{U^{\mathrm w}}8+\delta S\mathbf 1\{G=2\},
 \qquad
 \Delta Y_3=\frac{V^{\mathrm w}}8+\delta S\mathbf 1\{G=3\}.
\tag{Q3}
\]
Substitution of their cell means into the definition of \(q\) shows that all three retained conditional DDD contrasts equal \(\delta\).  The two target effects also equal \(\delta\), and therefore
\[
 q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)=0
 \quad\text{for every }(k,c)\in\mathcal I.
\tag{Q4}
\]
Put \(a=3/4\).  Every propensity ratio in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) equals one, and \(1/\pi_{2,1}=6\).  Substituting (Q3)--(Q4) into that definition gives the following complete conditional score table, in the coordinate order stated in the theorem:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w}).
\end{array}
\tag{Q5}
\]
Each row has conditional probability \(1/6\).  From the sign law,
\[
 E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]
 =E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
 \qquad
 E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\tag{Q6}
\]
Every column of (Q5) has conditional mean zero.  Multiplying the six rows coordinatewise, using \(E[(U^{\mathrm w})^2]=E[(V^{\mathrm w})^2]=1\) and (Q6), yields
\[
 \Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
 \begin{pmatrix}
 2&1&1\\
 1&2&2+xr\\
 1&2+xr&4+2xr
 \end{pmatrix}.
\tag{Q7}
\]
For example, its second--third entry is the sum of \(3/16\) from the cohort-two cells and \(3(1+xr)/16\) from the never-treated cells; its third diagonal is the sum of \(6/16\) and \(3(2+2xr)/16\).  These checks account for the shared-cell covariances.

Let \(B(x)=16\Gamma(x)/3\).  Its successive leading principal minors are
\[
 2,\qquad 3,\qquad \det B(x)=6-2x^2r^2=6-2r^2.
\tag{Q8}
\]
They are all positive because \(r^2<7/9<3\).  Gaussian elimination without row exchanges factors \(B(x)=L D L'\), where \(L\) is nonsingular and the diagonal pivots of \(D\) are the successive leading-minor ratios
\[
 2,\qquad \frac32,\qquad \frac{6-2r^2}{3}.
\]
All pivots are positive, so \(v'B(x)v=(L'v)'D(L'v)>0\) for every nonzero \(v\).  This proves the needed instance of Sylvester's criterion and shows that \(B(x)\), and hence \(\Gamma(x)\), is positive definite.  Since \(X\) has only two support points,
\[
 \min_{x\in\{-1,1\}}\lambda_{\min}\{\Gamma(x)\}>0
\tag{Q9}
\]
for each fixed admissible \(r\).  In addition, if \(d=(1,-1,0)'\), then \(d'\Gamma(x)d=3/8\).  Thus, up to the irrelevant sign of the one-column orthonormal basis \(N=d/\sqrt2\), \(H(x)=3/16\); the fixed-rank and positive-spectrum requirements used below hold.

The feasibility equations are \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\) and \(b_3=\omega_2\), so every feasible loading is uniquely
\[
 b(q)=\bigl(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2\bigr)'.
\tag{Q10}
\]
Using (Q7) and differentiating this scalar quadratic gives
\[
 \frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}
 =2d'\Gamma(x)b(q)
 =\frac34\left\{q-\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \frac{d^2}{dq^2}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac34.
\tag{Q11}
\]
The strict positivity of the second derivative proves
\[
 q^\star(x)=\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2},
 \qquad b^\star(x)=b\{q^\star(x)\}.
\tag{Q12}
\]
This also verifies the defining conditional quadratic program directly, without relying merely on the nonsingular formula in Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\).

Averaging (Q7) over the symmetric binary \(X\) deletes precisely the terms containing \(xr\).  Equation (Q11) then makes the unique best joint constant loading \(b(\omega_2/2)\).  The published componentwise rule instead minimizes the first target block using a covariance proportional to
\(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).  Subject to \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\), its unique minimum has \(b_1=b_2=\omega_1/2\); the singleton second block forces \(b_3=\omega_2\).  Hence
\[
 b^{\mathrm{const}}=b(\omega_2/2),
 \qquad b^{\mathrm{OVS}}=b(0).
\tag{Q13}
\]

The exact quadratic remainder from (Q11) is
\[
 E_P\!\left[b(q)'\Gamma(X)b(q)
 -b\{q^\star(X)\}'\Gamma(X)b\{q^\star(X)\}\right]
 =\frac38E_P\!\left[\left\{q-\frac{(1+Xr)\omega_2}{2}\right\}^2\right].
\tag{Q14}
\]
Since \(E_P[X]=0\) and \(E_P[X^2]=1\), this is
\[
 \frac38\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
 +\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q15}
\]

We finally establish that (Q15) is a loss relative to the published bound, rather than only to a selected score family.  At period two the published clean set is \(\{3,\infty\}\), so it produces the single nonzero row \((2,3,\infty)\); at period three its clean set is the singleton \(\{\infty\}\).  The localized construction has the same single row: target \((2,2)\) permits both comparisons, whereas target \((2,3)\) permits only \(\infty\).  The deterministic row conventions and the identical standardized-residual formula therefore give
\[
 Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty,P}.
\tag{Q16}
\]
Furthermore, direct subtraction of the first two columns of (Q5), with the common target-share correction canceling, gives
\[
 R_{(2,2),3,P}-R_{(2,2),\infty,P}=-Z_{2;3,\infty,P}.
\tag{Q17}
\]
The kernel of \(A'\) is spanned by \(d\), so (Q17) proves that \(\mathcal C_P\) is exactly the closed measurable span of the normal in (Q16).  The conditions for Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) were verified above; its two tangent-exhaustion identities now yield
\[
 \mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\tag{Q18}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(N'\Gamma(X)b^\star(X)=0\).  Since \(E_P[N'R_P\mid X]=0\), this says that \(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}=b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal C_P\), while its difference from \(\psi_P^0\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_P\).  Thus it is the residual from projecting \(\psi_P^0\) on \(\mathcal C_P\).  Uniqueness of orthogonal projections and (Q18) now imply
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}=\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P},
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P)=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}(P)=0.
\tag{Q19}
\]
Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) supplies the published-bound interpretation in (Q19), and Proposition \(\ref{prop:equality-frontier}\), together with (Q15), gives
\[
 \Delta\{b(q)\}
 =\frac38\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
 +\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q20}
\]
Substitution of the two values in (Q13) yields
\[
 \Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0,
 \qquad
 \Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\frac{3(1+r^2)\omega_2^2}{32}>0,
\tag{Q21}
\]
where strictness uses \(r>0\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\).  At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), these values are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\).  The first is the minimum over every deterministic feasible loading by the strict convexity in (Q11), completing the proof.

Because the collection of matrix maps is finite, it suffices first to treat one map and then intersect the resulting probability-one-asymptotic events.  Write \(B_0=B(z_0)\).  Continuous differentiability on a neighborhood of \(z_0\) gives a finite local Lipschitz constant, and \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) therefore implies
\[
 \|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(\tau_n).
\tag{S1}
\]
For completeness, the eigenvalue perturbation bound needed here follows directly from the variational characterization.  For every unit vector \(v\),
\[
 |v'\{B(\widehat z)-B_0\}v|
 \le \|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and applying this inequality inside the successive minimum--maximum formulas for the ordered eigenvalues gives
\[
 \max_k|\lambda_k\{B(\widehat z)\}-\lambda_k(B_0)|
 \le \|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{S2}
\]
With probability tending to one, the right side of (S2) is smaller than \(\tau_n\), while \(\tau_n<\kappa_0/2\).  On that event, every eigenvalue descending from the zero cluster has absolute value below \(\tau_n\), and every eigenvalue descending from a nonzero population eigenvalue has absolute value at least \(\kappa_0/2>\tau_n\).  Thus absolute-value thresholding recovers the population rank.  Finiteness of the collection proves simultaneous recovery.

We next construct the local differentiable inverse branch rather than assuming it.  Choose a positively oriented circle \(\gamma\) centered at zero whose interior contains no nonzero eigenvalue of \(B_0\).  Shrinking the neighborhood if necessary, the resolvent exists on \(\gamma\) and the same circle separates the eigenvalue cluster emanating from zero from all remaining eigenvalues.  Define
\[
 P_0(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_\gamma(wI-B(z))^{-1}\,dw.
\tag{S3}
\]
The resolvent identity
\[
 (wI-B_1)^{-1}-(wI-B_2)^{-1}
 =(wI-B_1)^{-1}(B_1-B_2)(wI-B_2)^{-1}
\tag{S4}
\]
and differentiation of the inverse show directly that \(P_0(z)\) is continuously differentiable.  Diagonalizing the real symmetric matrix \(B(z)\) inside the integrand shows coordinatewise that the integral is one on the separated small-eigenvalue cluster and zero on its complement.  Hence \(P_0(z)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto that cluster.  Set
\[
 B^\sharp(z)
 =(I-P_0(z))\{B(z)+P_0(z)\}^{-1}(I-P_0(z)).
\tag{S5}
\]
The middle matrix is nonsingular near \(z_0\): it acts as \(B(z)\) on the separated nonzero cluster and as \(B(z)+I\) on the small cluster.  Equations (S3)--(S5) therefore make \(B^\sharp\) continuously differentiable.  At \(z_0\) it equals \(B_0^\dagger\), and on the rank-recovery event it agrees with the thresholded inverse by zeroing the small cluster and inverting every retained eigenvalue.

To compute its derivative, decompose the Euclidean space orthogonally as \(\operatorname{range}(B_0)\oplus\ker(B_0)\).  In this basis write
\[
 B_0=\begin{pmatrix}D&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B_0^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}D^{-1}&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 H=\begin{pmatrix}H_{11}&H_{12}\\H_{21}&H_{22}\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(D\) is nonsingular.  Differentiating (S3)--(S5), block by block, gives
\[
 DB_0^\sharp[H]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 -D^{-1}H_{11}D^{-1}&D^{-2}H_{12}\\
 H_{21}D^{-2}&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\tag{S6}
\]
Multiplying the displayed block matrices verifies that (S6) is exactly
\[
 DB_0^\sharp[H]
 =-B_0^\dagger HB_0^\dagger
 +(B_0^\dagger)^2H(I-B_0B_0^\dagger)
 +(I-B_0^\dagger B_0)H(B_0^\dagger)^2.
\tag{S7}
\]

Every ordinary division appearing in \(F\) is continuously differentiable on a sufficiently small neighborhood because its denominator is nonzero at \(z_0\).  Equations (S5)--(S7), ordinary matrix calculus, and the chain rule thus show that the selected-rank composition \(F^\sharp\) is continuously differentiable at \(z_0\).  Its first-order expansion is
\[
 F^\sharp(\widehat z)-F^\sharp(z_0)
 =DF(z_0)'(\widehat z-z_0)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{S8}
\]
On the simultaneous rank-recovery event, \(F_{\tau_n}(\widehat z)=F^\sharp(\widehat z)\), while \(F^\sharp(z_0)=F(z_0)\).  Substitution into (S8) proves the claimed expansion and completes the proof.

Write the support of \(X\) as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\).  The separate support coordinates in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) give
\[
 P(X=x_d)=E_P[U_d^X].
\tag{W3}
\]
For every retained cell, positivity of the support mass and retained-cell overlap make the following denominators nonzero:
\[
 p_{a,s}(x_d)
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U_d^X]},
 \qquad
 m_{a,s,u}(x_d)
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(1,u)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]},
\tag{W4}
\]
and
\[
 E_P[\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_d]
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(2,u,v)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}.
\tag{W5}
\]
Because \(D\), \(T\), and \(\mathcal G\) are finite, (W3)--(W5) reconstruct all support masses, cell probabilities, first moments, and second cross-moments.  The formulas in the core then reconstruct \(\pi\), \(q\), \(\theta\), \(\Psi\), \(\Omega\), \(Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) as explicit functions of \(\mu(P)\).

The corrected score vector has mean zero.  Therefore the variance of the declared law-dependent comparator is
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}
 =b_z\{\mu(P)\}'\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b_z\{\mu(P)\}.
\tag{W6}
\]
Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) be the reference loading from Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\).  Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) and finite-support conditioning give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 &=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
 -E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)]\\
 &=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b^{\mathrm{ref}}
 -\sum_{d=1}^D P(X=x_d)
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)^\dagger
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{W7}
\]
Subtracting (W7) from (W6) is exactly formula (G4) defining \(F_z\).  This proves
\[
 F_z\{\mu(P)\}
 =\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P).
\tag{W8}
\]
In particular, the reconstruction differentiates the rule \(P\mapsto b_z(P)\); it does not incorrectly hold a numerical loading fixed while differentiating the law.

We next establish the stochastic order required by the selected-rank lemma.  The fourth-moment assumption and
\[
 |\Delta Y_u|^4\le 8(|Y_u|^4+|Y_{u-1}|^4),
 \qquad
 (\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v)^2
 \le\frac12\{(\Delta Y_u)^4+(\Delta Y_v)^4\}
\tag{W9}
\]
show that every coordinate of \(U(O)\) has a finite second moment.  Coordinatewise Chebyshev inequalities, combined over the fixed dimension \(d_\mu\), yield
\[
 \widehat\mu-\mu(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_U:=\operatorname{Var}_P\{U(O)\}<\infty.
\tag{W10}
\]

At the fixed law, there are only finitely many matrices \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)\) and comparator KKT matrices.  Each is real symmetric, and the minimum absolute value among all of their nonzero eigenvalues is strictly positive.  On the overlap domain their entries are continuously differentiable rational functions of \(\mu\); all ordinary denominators are nonzero by (W3)--(W5).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:fixed-support-selected-rank-delta}\), applied with \(z=\mu\), (W10), \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), therefore proves simultaneous population-rank recovery and
\[
 F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)-F_z\{\mu(P)\}
 =d_z'\{\widehat\mu-\mu(P)\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{W11}
\]
Since \(\widehat\mu-\mu(P)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n[U(O_i)-\mu(P)]\), equations (W8) and (W11) give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_z(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{W12}
\]
The summands are independent and identically distributed by the sampling assumption, have mean zero by definition, and have variance \(V_{\Delta,z}\in(0,\infty)\) by (W10) and the stated positivity condition.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\), followed by the elementary fact that adding an \(o_P(1)\) term preserves convergence at every continuity point, proves the normal limit in (W2).

It remains to prove variance consistency under the stated moments.  Rank recovery and continuity of the selected branch imply
\[
 \widehat d_z\longrightarrow_P d_z.
\tag{W13}
\]
For any entry \(W=U_jU_k\), \(E_P|W|<\infty\) by Cauchy--Schwarz and (W10).  Let \(W_M=W\mathbf 1\{|W|\le M\}\).  The sample average of bounded \(W_M\) converges in probability to its expectation by Chebyshev's inequality, while Markov's inequality gives, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 P\{\mathbb P_n|W-W_M|>\epsilon\}
 \le \epsilon^{-1}E_P[|W|\mathbf 1\{|W|>M\}].
\tag{W14}
\]
The right side tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Finiteness of the matrix dimension and \(\widehat\mu\to_P\mu(P)\) consequently imply
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}'
 \longrightarrow_P\Sigma_U.
\tag{W15}
\]
Premultiplying and postmultiplying (W15) by \(\widehat d_z\), and using (W13), gives
\[
 \widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
 \longrightarrow_P d_z'\Sigma_Ud_z=V_{\Delta,z}.
\tag{W16}
\]

Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) be the \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law.  Equations (W12) and (W16), with \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), imply
\[
 T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\]
so the interval
\[
 \left[\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}
 -z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n},\ 
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}
 +z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n}\right]
\]
has pointwise limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  Finally, (W12) gives \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and (W16) makes the half-width \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), their sum in absolute value is below \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.  The lower endpoint is then at least \(\delta_0/2\), as claimed.
